R. Q. 1 بَرْبَرَ , inf. n. بَرْبَرَةٌ, He talked much, and raised a clamour, or confused noise, (M, K,) with his tongue: (M:) he cried, or cried out, (S, K,) and talked in anger, (S,) or talked confusedly, with anger and aversion. (TA.) And بَرْبَرَ فِى كَلَامِهِ He was profuse and unprofitable in his talk. (Fr.) ―
-b2- Also, inf. n. as above, He (a goat) uttered a cry or cries, [or rattled,] (M, K,) being excited by desire of the female. (M.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
